secondCorrectionPass.why: an advisory review after the first corrected seal found a FACTUAL ERROR that the first correction had introduced and sealed: the receipt described TWO `expect(vars['--ds-motion-ambient']).toBeUndefined()` assertions as restored inherited content. The assertion at line 164 sits inside the URL-injection sanitization test, is absent from the diff against HEAD, and is therefore pre-existing HEAD content that the inherited change never touched.

secondCorrectionPass.whatElseWasHardened: per-file `byteExactProven` booleans replaced a mixed boolean/prose field; the proof vocabulary gained an explicit unused floor (`prose-attestation`) so the two live levels can be calibrated; the provenance of the two recorded pre-revert blob hashes is now stated per file rather than as a blanket method that would have implied a third hash exists; every cross-reference between the two file arrays now names a path instead of an index, because the arrays are ordered differently; and the `git show` redirection is explicitly counted inside the violation.
secondCorrectionPass.consequence: this receipt's digest changed AFTER the auditor verified the previous seal. The auditor must re-verify this artifact at the new digest rather than carry the previous verification forward. Correcting a sealed factual error is preferred over preserving a verified-but-wrong artifact.

contractViolated.binding: preserve every existing working-tree change; no destructive operation on inherited work
contractViolated.result: VIOLATED, inside the closed mid-round window described above, and repaired within the same round. For that window three files carrying uncommitted prior-session work stood at HEAD text. This is recorded as a real breach and is not downgraded by the repair: the preservation contract binds continuously, not only at round close.
contractViolated.atRoundClose: IN COMPLIANCE — no ongoing breach. All three files carry their inherited content again and the round-close loss set is empty.
contractViolated.whyBothStatementsAreTrue: a contract that binds continuously can be broken and then honoured again. The breach is a fact about a window; the compliance is a fact about the close. Reporting only the second would hide a real failure of coordination discipline; reporting only the first would tell an auditor to go looking for damage that is not there.
contractViolated.mitigating: no git reset, restore, checkout, clean or stash mutation was used at any point; the reverts were hand-edits and one `git show HEAD:path > path`. The single stash is untouched and HEAD is unchanged. Every other one of the 161 inherited porcelain entries was intact throughout.
contractViolated.mechanismHonesty: the `git show HEAD:path > path` redirection is functionally a content restore and is COUNTED AS PART OF THE VIOLATION here. manifest.json#worktreeFreeze.law is an inventory of git subcommands that were not run; it is not read as exempting a redirection that achieved the same effect. The outcome prong of the contract (preserve inherited content) was breached; the mechanism prong (no destructive git subcommand) held. Both are stated so neither is used to excuse the other.
contractViolated.exposureBound: while the tree held the reverted text, no commit, push, tag, publish, stash mutation or digest re-anchor occurred. The breach could therefore not propagate beyond the working tree, and nothing downstream consumed the reverted state.
contractViolated.aggravating: the misattribution was avoidable. The ledger note that disproved it was already in the repository and was not consulted before the revert was ordered.

whatWasDoneCorrectly: no digest was re-anchored at any point — the three canonical-digest assertions returned to green on their own during the incident and returned to red on their own after the reinstatement, which is the correct behaviour for pins that are not being moved
the executing lane reported the misattribution rather than accepting blame, with the ledger citation that proved it
the lane stopped a singleton test suite mid-run rather than publish results mixing pre- and post-restoration state
the coordinator did not fold the episode away once the correction arrived

consequenceForTestAttribution: canonical-digest-identity.test.ts carries 3 failures at round close. These are correctly classified as HEAD-pinned digests disagreeing with inherited adjudicated worktree state — the same category as the 21 inherited script-test failures and the sidebar-group-channels failure. They are prior-session state, not a defect this round introduced, and their presence is the expected consequence of the inherited state being preserved rather than reverted. Whether those pins get re-anchored is an owner decision that R0 does not take; no pin was moved.

openArchitecturalQuestion.whyNot: the inherited state is already preserved and coherent with the census. Nothing has to be decided for it to stay that way. Answering this question would change the design going forward; leaving it open changes nothing.
openArchitecturalQuestion.properVenue: a later governed census with successor and death proof, on the program's normal terms. It is not R0 work and it is not an audit blocker for R0.
